title.en: The Call of Abram

region.en: Haran to Shechem, land of Canaan

texts.period: Genesis 12, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 12

summary.en: The LORD tells the seventy-five-year-old Abram to leave country, kindred, and father's house for a land he will be shown, promising to make of him a great nation through whom all families of the earth will be blessed. Abram goes, builds altars at Shechem and Bethel, and Christian tradition sees in this migration the founding charter of the pilgrim people of God.
summary.zh: 耶和華對七十五歲的亞伯蘭說：要離開本地、本族、父家，往所指示之地去；應許使他成大國，萬族因他得福。亞伯蘭遵命而行，在示劍、伯特利築壇。基督教傳統視此遷徙為朝聖之民、因信而行之始。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared by Judaism and Christianity. Presented as a founding-migration narrative.

passages.text: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee: and I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: and I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed. So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him.

And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan; and into the land of Canaan they came. And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh. And the LORD appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the LORD, who appeared unto him.

title.en: Abram's Sister-Wife Deception in Egypt

texts.period: Genesis 12, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 12

summary.en: Famine drives Abram to Egypt, where he passes Sarai off as his sister to save his own life; Pharaoh takes her into his house and rewards Abram richly, until plagues fall on the court and the truth is out. The king sends them away unharmed — the first of the twice-told 'sister-wife' tales in which the patriarchs' survival cunning is ironically preserved by the outsiders they deceive.
summary.zh: 饑荒使亞伯蘭下埃及；他懼死，謊稱撒萊為妹。法老娶她入宮，厚賜亞伯蘭；耶和華卻降大災於法老全家。真相既明，法老遣之而去，毫髮無傷——此乃族長「妹妻」雙重敘事之首，倖存之機巧反由受騙的外邦人保全。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a deception-survival tale type; scholarly framing.

passages.text: And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there. And it came to pass, when he was come near to enter into Egypt, that he said unto Sarai his wife, Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon: therefore it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they shall say, This is his wife: and they will kill me, but they will save thee alive. Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee.

The princes also of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her before Pharaoh: and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house. And he entreated Abram well for her sake. And the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram's wife. And Pharaoh called Abram and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife? now therefore behold thy wife, take her, and go thy way.

title.en: Melchizedek Blesses Abram

region.zh: 王谷，撒冷（耶路撒冷）附近

texts.period: Genesis 14, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 14

summary.en: When four eastern kings plunder Sodom and carry off Lot, Abram arms his 318 trained servants, strikes them by night, and brings back all the goods and people. Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings out bread and wine and blesses the victor, who gives him a tenth of all — a mysterious priest-king whom Christian tradition (in Hebrews 7) reads as a figure of Christ, the eternal priest, and whose bread and wine echo the Eucharist.
summary.zh: 四王擄掠所多瑪，擄走羅得；亞伯蘭率三百一十八名家丁夜襲，救回人財。撒冷王、至高神的祭司麥基洗德攜餅與酒而出，為他祝福；亞伯蘭將所得十分之一獻上。基督教《希伯來書》以此無譜之王為基督永恆祭司的預表，餅酒亦隱合聖餐。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Melchizedek's Christological reading (Hebrews 7) is noted; presented as a comparative sacred-kingship narrative.

passages.text: And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew; for he dwelt in the plain of Mamre. And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan. And he divided himself against them, he and his servants, by night, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah. And he brought back all the goods, and also brought again his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.

And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God. And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth: and blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all. And the king of Sodom said unto Abram, Give me the persons, and take the goods to thyself. And Abram said, I will not take from a thread even to a shoelatchet, and that I will not take any thing that is thine.

title.en: The Covenant Between the Pieces

texts.period: Genesis 15, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 15

summary.en: In a vision the childless Abram is told his heir will come from his own body and his seed will be as the stars; 'he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness' — the verse Paul makes the cornerstone of justification by faith. Sealing the covenant, Abram cuts the sacrificial animals, falls into a dread darkness, and a smoking furnace and burning lamp pass between the pieces, while prophecy of 400 years of servitude in a strange land is spoken.
summary.zh: 異象中，無子的亞伯蘭得諭：後裔將自其身而出，多如眾星；「亞伯蘭信耶和華，耶和華就以此為他的義」——保羅因信稱義之基石經文。獻祭牲剖分兩半，亞伯蘭沉睡於大黑暗；冒煙的爐並燒著的火把從肉塊中經過，立約為憑，並預言四百年寄居異邦。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Paul's faith-righteousness reading (Romans 4) is the classic Christian use of this text.

passages.text: After these things the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward. And Abram said, LORD God, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless? And, behold, the word of the LORD came unto him, saying, This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

And he said unto him, Take me an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon. And he took unto him all these, and divided them in the midst, and laid each piece one against another. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces. In the same day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land.

title.en: Hagar in the Wilderness

region.zh: 書珥曠野，庇耳拉海萊井

texts.period: Genesis 16 and 21, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 16 and 21

summary.en: Barren Sarai gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram as wife; conceiving, Hagar flees her mistress's harshness into the wilderness, where the angel of the LORD finds her by a spring, promises a countless seed, and names her son Ishmael — 'thou God seest me,' she says, naming the well Beerlahairoi. Cast out later with her son, she sits a bowshot off weeping that she may not see the child die, until God opens her eyes to a well and makes of Ishmael a great nation.
summary.zh: 撒萊使埃及使女夏甲與亞伯蘭同房；夏甲有孕後被苦待而逃至曠野。耶和華的使者在泉旁尋見她，應許後裔無數，並為其子命名以實瑪利；她稱那井為庇耳拉海萊——「看顧人的神」。後母子被逐，坐泣於一箭之遙，神開她的眼得見水井，以實瑪利終成大國。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared with Islam (Ishmael as Arab ancestor). Presented comparatively with sensitivity to both traditions.

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur. And he said, Hagar, Sarai's maid, whence camest thou? and whither wilt thou go? And she said, I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai. And the angel of the LORD said unto her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands. And the angel of the LORD said unto her, I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.

Behold, thou art with child and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael; because the LORD hath heard thy affliction. And she called the name of the LORD that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me? Wherefore the well was called Beerlahairoi.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of water, and gave it unto Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and the child, and sent her away: and she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba. And she went, and sat her down over against him a good way off, as it were a bow shot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And God heard the voice of the lad; and God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink.

title.en: Abraham, the Everlasting Covenant, and Isaac Promised
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕、永約與以撒之諾

region.en: Canaan, at the oaks of Mamre

texts.period: Genesis 17, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 17

summary.en: When Abram is ninety-nine, God Almighty appears, renames him Abraham — 'father of many nations' — establishes the everlasting covenant sealed in the flesh by circumcision on the eighth day, renames Sarai Sarah, and promises that the ninety-year-old Sarah will bear a son named Isaac with whom the covenant will stand. Abraham falls on his face and laughs; Christian tradition reads the covenant as fulfilled spiritually in Christ, 'the seed of Abraham', in whom all nations are blessed.
summary.zh: 亞伯蘭九十九歲時，全能的神向他顯現，改名亞伯拉罕——「多國之父」——立永約，以割禮為約之記號；撒萊改名撒拉，並應許九十歲的她將生以撒，約要在以撒身上堅立。亞伯拉罕俯伏在地喜笑。基督教傳統視此約在基督——亞伯拉罕的後裔——身上成全，萬國因之得福。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition shared by Judaism and Christianity (and echoed in Islam). Circumcision covenant presented as ritual-origin narrative.

passages.text: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, the LORD appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect. And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly. Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee. And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant.

This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised. And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you. And God said unto Abraham, As for Sarai thy wife, thou shalt not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be. And I will bless her, and give thee a son also of her: yea, I will bless her, and she shall be a mother of nations; kings of people shall be of her.

Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear? And God said, Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son indeed; and thou shalt call his name Isaac: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.

title.en: The Three Visitors and Sarah's Laughter

region.en: Tent door at the plains of Mamre

texts.period: Genesis 18, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 18

summary.en: In the heat of the day Abraham entertains three men under a tree with cakes, a dressed calf, butter, and milk — one of whom is the LORD. They announce that Sarah, past the age of women, will bear a son; Sarah laughs within the tent and denies it, and is told 'Is any thing too hard for the LORD?' Christian iconography reads the three strangers as a foreshadowing of the Trinity, and the episode as the great Old Testament exemplar of hospitality.
summary.zh: 天正熱時，亞伯拉罕以餅、犢、奶油牛奶款待帳棚前的三位客人——其中一位乃是耶和華。他們宣告年老停經的撒拉將生子；撒拉在帳棚內暗笑，被告知「耶和華豈有難成的事麼？」。基督教聖像畫以三客預示三位一體，此事亦為舊約款待之範式。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Trinitarian reading is a Christian interpretive tradition, noted here; the text itself is Jewish scripture.

passages.text: And the LORD appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre: and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day; and he lift up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood by him: and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself toward the ground, and said, My LORD, if now I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant. And Abraham hastened into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal.

And they said unto him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent. And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him. Now Abraham and Sarah were old and well stricken in age; and it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women. Therefore Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?

And the LORD said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I of a surety bear a child, which am old? Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son. Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh.

title.en: Sodom Overthrown, Lot's Wife a Pillar of Salt
title.zh: 所多瑪傾覆，羅得妻成鹽柱

region.en: Cities of the plain, south Dead Sea (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 平原諸城，死海南端（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Genesis 19, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 19

summary.en: Two angels lodge with Lot in Sodom; the city's men besiege the door demanding the strangers, and Lot offers his daughters in vain before the angels strike the mob blind. At dawn Lot's family is dragged from the city — 'escape for thy life; look not behind thee' — and fire and brimstone rain from the LORD upon Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. In a cave the daughters make their father drunk and bear Moab and Benammi, founders of Israel's neighboring nations.
summary.zh: 二天使夜宿羅得家；所多瑪人圍門索人，羅得欲以二女代之，天使使眾人眼盲。黎明羅得一家被拉出城——「逃命吧，不可回頭看」——耶和華降硫磺與火；羅得妻回顧，變成鹽柱。後二女於山洞灌醉其父，生摩押與便亞米，即以色列二鄰族之祖。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Presented as a destruction-and-refugee narrative with an incest-founding etiology; later interpretive uses of the Sodom story vary widely and are not endorsed here.

passages.text: But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter: and they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them. And Lot went out at the door unto them, and shut the door after him, and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. But the men put forth their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut to the door.

And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters, which are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city. And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city. And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain.

Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven; and he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground. But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt. And Abraham gat up early in the morning to the place where he stood before the LORD: and he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and, lo, the smoke of the country went up as the smoke of a furnace.

title.en: The Binding of Isaac

texts.period: Genesis 22, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 22

summary.en: God tests Abraham: 'Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest... and offer him there for a burnt offering.' On the third day father and son climb Mount Moriah, Isaac bearing the wood and asking where the lamb is; Abraham binds him on the altar and raises the knife before the angel's cry stays his hand, and a ram caught by its horns is offered in the son's place. Christian tradition reads the akedah as a type of the Father's sacrifice of the Son — God who provides himself a lamb.
summary.zh: 神試驗亞伯拉罕：「帶著你的兒子，就是你獨生的兒子，你愛的以撒……把他獻為燔祭。」三日後父子登摩利亞山，以撒背柴，問燔祭的羊羔在哪裏；亞伯拉罕築壇綁子，舉刀欲殺，天使呼叫止手，公羊以角掛於稠密小樹代獻。基督教傳統以此預表聖父犧牲聖子——神必自己預備羔羊。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Judaism and Christianity, both of which hold the akedah as a foundational text of tested faith; the Christian typological reading is noted.

passages.text: And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am. And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of. And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering.

And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering? And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together. And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood. And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.

And the angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I. And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me. And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.

title.en: Abraham Buys the Cave of Machpelah

region.zh: 希伯崙（基列亞巴），迦南地

texts.period: Genesis 23, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 23

summary.en: Sarah dies at Hebron at 127, and the wandering Abraham, 'a stranger and a sojourner' among the Hittites, negotiates publicly at the city gate for Ephron's field and the cave of Machpelah, paying 400 shekels of silver — the patriarchs' only owned piece of the promised land, where Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, and (by Jacob's wish) Jacob are buried. The site remains a shrine to this day, shared and contested.
summary.zh: 撒拉於希伯崙享壽一百二十七歲而終。寄居異地的亞伯拉罕在城門口眾人面前，以四百舍客勒銀子購以弗崙田間的麥比拉洞——族長在應許之地唯一的產業。亞伯拉罕、撒拉、以撒、利百加、利亞並雅各皆葬於此。聖地至今仍是共享而紛爭不斷之所。

sensitivity.note: The Hebron tomb remains a live religious site for Jews and Muslims; the record covers only the ancient narrative.

passages.text: And Sarah was an hundred and seven and twenty years old: these were the years of the life of Sarah. And Sarah died in Kirjatharba; the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her. And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spake unto the sons of Heth, saying, I am a stranger and a sojourner with you: give me a possession of a buryingplace with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.

And Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, saying, Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that is therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the sons of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead. And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. And the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace.

title.en: Rebekah at the Well

region.zh: 拿鶴城，美索不達米亞（哈蘭一帶）

texts.period: Genesis 24, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 24

summary.en: Abraham sends his eldest servant sworn by the LORD to find Isaac a wife from his own kindred; at the evening well the servant prays for a sign — the girl who offers water to him and his ten camels — and before he finishes speaking Rebekah arrives and does exactly that. Betrothal gifts, Laban's welcome, her decisive 'I will go', and Isaac's taking her into Sarah's tent close the longest and gentlest chapter in Genesis.
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕遣老僕起誓，回本族為以撒娶妻。僕人至井旁禱告求記號——凡遞水予他並十駝飲者即所選之女。話未完，利百加出現，恰如此行。聘禮既下，利百加說「我去」，與以撒相遇於暮色田野，入撒拉帳棚成婚，以撒得安慰。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The well sign is a divination-adjacent test, tagged as oracle-divination with that interpretive caveat.

passages.text: And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh: and I will make thee swear by the LORD, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell: but thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.

And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water. And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day. And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac.

And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder. And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up. And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink. And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.

title.en: Jacob and Esau: Birthright for Pottage
title.zh: 雅各與以掃：長子名分換紅湯

texts.period: Genesis 25, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 25

summary.en: Rebekah's twins struggle in her womb; the oracle answers 'two nations are in thy womb, and the elder shall serve the younger'. Esau is born red and hairy, Jacob grasping his heel; the hunter and the quiet tent-dweller divide their parents' love, and one famished evening Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of red lentil pottage, 'thus Esau despised his birthright.'
summary.zh: 利百加腹中雙子相爭，神諭答曰：「兩國在你腹內……將來大的要服事小的。」以掃渾身有毛而紅，雅各手抓其踵。善獵者與安靜帳棚者各得父母偏愛；一日以掃打獵困乏，以紅豆湯將長子名分賣給雅各——「以掃輕看了他長子的名分」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The twin-oracle tag of sibling-creators is interpretive — the pair found rival nations (Israel and Edom), noted here.

passages.text: And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren: and Rebekah his wife conceived. And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the LORD. And the LORD said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.

And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb. And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau. And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob. And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. Now Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.

And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint: and Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint. And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright. And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; thus Esau despised his birthright.

title.en: Jacob Steals the Firstborn Blessing

texts.period: Genesis 27, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 27

summary.en: Blind old Isaac, wanting venison before blessing Esau, is outmaneuvered by Rebekah: Jacob brings kid-meat dressed as game, goatskins cover his smooth hands and neck, and the dying-speech blessing is irrevocably given — 'the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.' Esau returns to a bitter cry that cannot be undone; Isaac gives him a lesser doom of the sword and the wilderness, and Esau resolves to kill Jacob.
summary.zh: 老眼昏花的以撒欲食野味後祝福以掃，利百加設計：雅各仿野味烹羊羔，羊皮裹手貼頸。祝福出口不可挽回——「聲音是雅各的聲音，手卻是以掃的手」。以掃歸來放聲大哭，只得次等命定：靠刀劍度日；遂懷恨欲殺雅各，雅各亡命哈蘭。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as the classic doomed-blessing (irrevocable word) tale; the moral ambiguity of the deception is part of the text's long interpretive history.

passages.text: And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying, Bring me venison, and make me savoury meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the LORD before my death. Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee. Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for thy father, such as he loveth: and thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may bless thee before his death.

And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son: and she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck. And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy first born. And Isaac said, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son. And Jacob went near; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. And he discerned him not; so he blessed him.

And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed: therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine: let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee. And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

title.en: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel

region.en: Bethel (Luz), on the road to Haran
region.zh: 伯特利（路斯），往哈蘭路上

texts.period: Genesis 28, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 28

summary.en: Fleeing Esau, Jacob sleeps on a stone at a nameless place and dreams of a ladder set on earth whose top reaches heaven, angels ascending and descending, and the LORD standing above it promising land, countless seed, and safe return. Waking, he cries 'Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not', sets the stone up as a pillar, anoints it, and names the place Bethel, the house of God — vowing the tenth and, in Christian reading, seeing in the ladder Christ the bridge between heaven and earth (John 1:51).
summary.zh: 雅各逃離以掃，枕石而臥，夢見天梯立地通天，神的使者上去下來，耶和華立於梯上應許土地、後裔與平安歸回。醒來呼曰：「耶和華真在這裏，我竟不知道！」遂立石為柱、澆油其上，名其地為伯特利——神的家。基督教釋經以梯喻基督，天地之間的橋（約翰福音一51）。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The ladder-as-Christ reading is the Christian interpretive tradition, noted here.

passages.text: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep. And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I am the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed.

And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of. And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not. And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven. And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it. And he called the name of that place Bethel.

title.en: Seven Years for Rachel, Deceived by Leah
title.zh: 為拉結服事七年，被利亞所欺

region.en: Haran, land of the people of the east

texts.period: Genesis 29-30, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 29-30

summary.en: At Haran's well Jacob rolls away the stone, kisses Rachel, and weeps; he serves Laban seven years for her, 'and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her' — only to wake after the wedding feast and find Leah, veiled, in the dark. He gains Rachel a week later by serving seven years more. The two rival wives and their maids bear the twelve sons of Israel, Leah's womb opened because she was hated and Rachel's at last with Joseph.
summary.zh: 雅各在哈蘭井旁推石飲羊，吻拉結而哭；為她服事拉班七年，「因深愛拉結，就看這七年如同幾天」——婚宴翌晨才發現黑暗中竟是利亞。再服七年始得拉結。二妻與二使女為他生下以色列十二支派；利亞因失寵而蒙眷顧，拉結終生約瑟。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Deceiver deceived; the divine-marriage tag is loose (a marriage-quest narrative), noted here.

passages.text: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep; for she kept them. And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother. And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept. And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was Rebekah's son: and she ran and told her father.

And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter. And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me. And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her. And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me?

And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn. Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also for the service which thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years. And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years. And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren. And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb. And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, God hath taken away my reproach: and she called his name Joseph.

title.en: The Flight from Laban and the Mizpah Covenant
title.zh: 逃離拉班與米斯巴之約

region.en: Mount Gilead, east of the Jordan

texts.period: Genesis 31, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 31

summary.en: Told by God to return, Jacob slips away while Laban is shearing sheep; Rachel steals her father's household gods and hides them in camel's furniture, sitting on them and pleading the custom of women. Warned in a dream, Laban pursues, searches, finds nothing, and the two raise a heap of stones — Galeed and Mizpah — swearing the LORD watch between them when they are absent one from another.
summary.zh: 神諭雅各歸回，趁拉班剪羊毛之際潛逃；拉結偷了父親家中的神像，藏於駱駝馱簍，坐在其上託詞「身上不便」。拉班夢中被神警告，追及基列，搜遍帳棚而不得。二人累石為證，立約於米斯巴——「願耶和華在你我中間鑒察」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Boundary-covenant etiology of the Mizpah heap.

passages.text: And Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives upon camels; and he carried away all his cattle, and all his goods which he had gotten, for to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan. And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's. And Jacob stole away unawares to Laban the Syrian, in that he told him not that he fled.

And it was told Laban on the third day that Jacob was fled. And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days' journey; and they overtook him in the mount Gilead. And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night, and said unto him, Take heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad. And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father's house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?

Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel's furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not. And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched but found not the images. Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee. And Mizpah; for he said, The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.

title.en: Jacob Wrestles at Peniel

texts.period: Genesis 32-33, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 32-33

summary.en: Sick with fear of Esau's four hundred men, Jacob sends everything across the Jabbok and is left alone; a man wrestles with him till daybreak, touches the hollow of his thigh, and blesses him when Jacob will not let go — 'thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.' Jacob calls the place Peniel, 'for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved', and limps for life; the children of Israel do not eat the sinew that shrank. The next day the brothers embrace and weep.
summary.zh: 雅各懼以掃四百人，將家眷財物渡過雅博河，獨自留下；有個人與他摔跤直到黎明，摸其大腿窩，雅各緊抓不放求祝福——「你的名不要再叫雅各，要叫以色列，因為你與神與人較力，都得了勝。」雅各名其地為毗努伊勒：「我面對面見了神，我的性命仍得保全」，從此瘸腿；以色列人不吃大腿窩的筋。翌日兄弟相擁而泣。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The name-change and the food prohibition are the ritual-origin elements; interpretive traditions differ on who the wrestler is.

passages.text: And he rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two womenservants, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford Jabbok. And he took them, and sent them over the brook, and sent over that he had. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.

And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed. And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved. And as he passed over Penuel the sun rose upon him, and he halted upon his thigh.

And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother. And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept. And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; keep that thou hast unto thyself. And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found grace in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand.

title.en: Dinah and the Massacre of Shechem

texts.period: Genesis 34, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 34

summary.en: Shechem, the Hivite prince's son, takes and defiles Dinah, then loves her and asks for her in marriage. Jacob's sons answer deceitfully: all the men of the city consent to circumcision as the price of intermarriage; on the third day, while they are sore, Simeon and Levi put the city to the sword, spoil it, and carry off wives, children, and wealth. Jacob fears the land will rise against him; his sons answer coldly, 'Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?'
summary.zh: 示劍玷污底拿，後因愛她求婚。雅各眾子以詭詐回答：全城男丁為通婚受割禮；第三日眾人疼痛之際，西緬與利未提劍屠城，擄掠財物婦孺。雅各懼迦南人聚集攻滅全家，眾子冷冷回答：「他豈可待我們的妹子如同妓女麼？」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a violation-and-vengeance narrative; the massacre is presented without endorsement, and Jacob's rebuke is part of the text.

passages.text: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land. And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her. And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel. And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to wife.

And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, because he had defiled Dinah their sister: We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us: but in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we be, that every male of you be circumcised. And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised.

And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males. And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and went out. The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city, because they had defiled their sister. And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land.

title.en: Tamar and the Pledges of Judah

region.zh: 往亭拿路上，亞杜蘭附近

texts.period: Genesis 38, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 38

summary.en: Er dies, Onan refuses to raise up seed to his brother and dies, and Judah withholds young Shelah from Tamar — so Tamar veils herself as a shrine prostitute at the road gate, takes Judah's signet, bracelets, and staff as pledge, and conceives. Accused of harlotry and dragged out to be burned, she produces the pledges: 'she hath been more righteous than I,' Judah admits. Of the twins Pharez and Zarah, Pharez carries the line to David — and, in Matthew's genealogy, to Jesus.
summary.zh: 珥死，俄南不肯為兄立後而死，猶大又扣下示拉；他瑪遂蒙面扮妓，坐在往亭拿的路口，取猶大的印、帶子與杖為當頭而懷孕。被告淫亂拉出要燒時，她出示信物；猶大說：「她比我更有義。」其孿生子法勒斯攜猶大支派血統至大衛，馬太福音家譜更達於耶穌。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Levirate law and pledge-trickery narrative; the messianic lineage reading (Matthew 1) is noted.

passages.text: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar. And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD slew him. And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother. And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother. And the thing which he did displeased the LORD: wherefore he slew him also.

And she put her widow's garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife. When Judah saw her, he thought her to be an harlot; because she had covered her face. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it? And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that is in thine hand. And he gave it her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.

And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter in law hath played the harlot; and also, behold, she is with child by whoredom. And Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt. When she was brought forth, she sent to her father in law, saying, By the man, whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and bracelets, and staff. And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.

title.en: Joseph's Dreams and the Coat in the Pit
title.zh: 約瑟的夢與坑中的彩衣

texts.period: Genesis 37, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 37

summary.en: Israel's coat of many colours marks his love for Joseph, and the seventeen-year-old's two dreams — sheaves bowing to his sheaf, sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him — sharpen the brothers' hatred. Sent to check on them at Dothan, he is stripped, thrown into a dry pit, and sold by Judah's counsel to Ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver; the brothers dip the coat in goat's blood, and Jacob refuses comfort, 'I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning.'
summary.zh: 以色列為約瑟作彩衣，十七歲的少年連得二夢——禾捆下拜，日月十一星下拜——招致兄長嫉恨。奉父命赴多坍探望，兄長們剝其彩衣，投之於無水的坑，經猶大提議，以二十舍客勒銀子賣給以實瑪利商人。眾兄以羊羔血染彩衣，雅各不肯受安慰：「我必悲哀著下陰間到我兒子那裏。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The dreams function as true prophecy in the narrative arc.

passages.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours. And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him. And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren: and they hated him yet the more. For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.

And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me. And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth? And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.

And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him. And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him. And they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him: and they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it. And Judah said unto his brethren, Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites. And they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

title.en: Joseph and Potiphar's Wife

texts.period: Genesis 39, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 39

summary.en: Sold to Potiphar, captain of Pharaoh's guard, Joseph prospers so that all his master's house is blessed through him; made overseer of everything, he refuses the master's wife day by day — 'how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?' — until, catching her grip on his garment, he flees leaving it in her hand. Her false cry convicts him before her husband, and the innocent slave is cast into the prison where the king's prisoners are bound.
summary.zh: 約瑟被賣給法老的內臣波提乏，事事蒙福，治理全家；卻日日拒絕主母——「我怎能作這大惡，得罪神呢？」終有一日，主母抓其衣裳，他棄衣而逃。主母誣告，主人怒而將無辜的奴隸下在監裏，與王的囚犯同囚。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Chastity-falsely-accused tale type; the trickster tag applies to the wife's deception.

passages.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites. And his master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand. And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me. But he refused, and said unto his master's wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand; there is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?

And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out. That she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us. And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home. And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison. But the LORD was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

title.en: The Butler's Dream in Pharaoh's Prison

region.en: Prison of the captain of the guard, Egypt

texts.period: Genesis 40, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 40

summary.en: Pharaoh's chief butler and baker offend him and are bound in Joseph's prison; both dream, and Joseph — 'Do not interpretations belong to God?' — reads the vine with three branches as three days to restoration, and the three white baskets eaten by birds as three days to hanging. All falls out on Pharaoh's birthday; yet the restored butler forgets Joseph for two full years.
summary.zh: 法老的酒政與膳長得罪主人被囚，同夜各得一夢。約瑟說「解夢不是出於神麼」——葡萄三枝即三日復職，頭上三筐白餅被飛鳥吃盡即三日被掛。果然應驗於法老生日；然而復職的酒政竟忘了約瑟，一忘兩年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Dream-interpretation narrative.

passages.text: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison. And Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and looked upon them, and, behold, they were sad. And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.

In my dream, behold, a vine was before me; and in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes: and Pharaoh's cup was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand. And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days: yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thy place.

When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white baskets on my head: and in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of bakemeats for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head. And Joseph answered and said, This is the interpretation thereof: The three baskets are three days: yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee. And it came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday. Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.

title.en: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph as Vizier

texts.period: Genesis 41, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 41

summary.en: Two years on, Pharaoh dreams of seven fat kine devoured by seven lean kine and of seven full ears blasted by seven thin, and none of Egypt's magicians can read it. The butler remembers Joseph, who is brought from the dungeon, shaved and changed, and declares 'It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace' — seven years plenty, then seven years famine. Pharaoh sets the ring on Joseph's hand, clothes him in fine linen, names him Zaphnathpaaneah, and rides him in the second chariot; the storehouses of Egypt are filled against the famine.
summary.zh: 兩年後，法老夢見七肥牛被七瘦牛所吞，七好穗被七枯穗所滅；埃及術士皆不能解。酒政想起約瑟，遂自監中提出，剃頭換衣入宮。約瑟說：「這不在乎我，神必將平安的話回答法老。」——七豐年後七荒年。法老將手上戒指戴在約瑟手上，賜名撒發那忒巴內亞，使其乘副車巡行埃及全地，倉廩囤糧以備荒年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The foreign vizier narrative; the second-chariot investiture is the kingship element.

passages.text: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river. And, behold, there came up out of the river seven well favoured kine and fatfleshed; and they fed in a meadow. And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill favoured and leanfleshed; and the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. And he slept and dreamed the second time: and, behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good; and, behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them.

Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day. And there was there with us a young man, an Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; and it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was. Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.

And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace. The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one. Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land. Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.

And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is? And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art: thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou. And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck; and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee.

title.en: The Silver Cup in Benjamin's Sack

texts.period: Genesis 42-44, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 42-44

summary.en: When ten brothers bow before the governor of Egypt begging corn, they do not know him, but he remembers his dreams and tests them: Simeon bound, corn returned with their money, Benjamin demanded. On the second visit Joseph weeps in private at the sight of his brother, feasts them, then hides his silver divining cup in Benjamin's sack; the cup is 'found', Judah offers himself as surety — 'let thy servant abide instead of the lad' — and the trap of mercy is sprung.
summary.zh: 十個哥哥向埃及宰相俯伏糴糧，不識其人，約瑟卻記得幼年的夢，並試驗他們：捆西緬、還銀糧、索便雅憫。再來時，約瑟見幼弟而暗自飲泣，設宴款待，又將銀杯藏於便雅憫袋中；搜出後，猶大以己身代之——「求你容僕人住下，替這童子作我主的奴僕」——憐憫的網羅已然張開。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The cup is used for divination in the narrative detail; tagged accordingly.

passages.text: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another? And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us from thence. And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph's brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth. And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them; and he remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them.

And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there. And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth. And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack. And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack. Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city. And Judah said, What shall we say unto my lord? Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren. For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad be not with me?

title.en: I Am Joseph: Reunion in Goshen

texts.period: Genesis 45-46, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 45-46

summary.en: Unable to restrain himself before all his retinue, Joseph cries 'Cause every man to go out from me' and reveals himself weeping aloud — 'I am Joseph; doth my father yet live?' He forgives: 'ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to save much people alive.' Pharaoh sends wagons, the stunned Jacob's spirit revives, and at Beersheba God appears to Israel in visions of the night promising to go down with him and bring him up again. Father and son fall on each other's necks in Goshen.
summary.zh: 約瑟在隨從面前不能再自禁，喊道「人都要離開我出去」，放聲大哭表明身份：「我是約瑟！我父親還在麼？」他饒恕他們：「從前你們的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的，要保全許多人的性命。」法老遣車接眷；雅各聞言心裏甦醒，在別是巴夜間異象中得神應許同行下埃及。父子在歌珊相擁而泣。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The descent into Egypt founds the Israel-in-Egypt cycle that Exodus continues.

passages.text: Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known unto his brethren. And he wept aloud: and the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard. And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.

And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life. So now it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.

And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices unto the God of his father Isaac. And God spake unto Israel in the visions of the night, and said, Jacob, Jacob. And he said, Here am I. And he said, I am God, the God of thy father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation: I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again.

title.en: Jacob's Last Words: The Sceptre of Judah

region.en: Jacob's bed, land of Goshen, Egypt

texts.period: Genesis 47-49, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 47-49

summary.en: Gathering his twelve sons at his deathbed 'to tell you that which shall befall you in the last days', Jacob blesses and characterizes each tribe in turn: Reuben unstable as water, Simeon and Levi scattered for the massacre, Judah a lion's whelp of whom 'the sceptre shall not depart... until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be' — the verse Christian tradition reads messianically of Christ — and Joseph the fruitful bough of double blessing. He charges burial in Machpelah and dies, and is mourned by all Egypt seventy days.
summary.zh: 臨終召集十二子「把你們日後必遇的事告訴你們」：流便如水滾沸不得居首，西緬利未因屠城分散，猶大如小獅——「圭必不離猶大，杖必不離他兩腳之間，直等細羅來到，萬民都必歸順」——基督教傳統以此為彌賽亞基督之預言；約瑟則是多結果子的樹枝，蒙雙倍祝福。遺命葬麥比拉洞，埃及為其哀哭七十日。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Shiloh verse is one of the most contested messianic readings in scripture; the Christian tradition's reading is noted alongside the tribal-blessing frame.

passages.text: And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days. Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power: unstable as water, thou shalt not excel. Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations. O my soul, come not thou into their secret; for in their anger they slew a man, and in their selfwill they digged down a wall.

Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee. Judah is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up? The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall: the archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him: but his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob. Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil. All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: and this is it that their father spake unto them, and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them.

title.en: The Mourning of Egypt and Joseph's Bones

region.en: Goshen to Machpelah, funeral road beyond Jordan
region.zh: 歌珊至麥比拉洞，約旦河外送葬之路

texts.period: Genesis 50, patriarchal cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 50

summary.en: Joseph embalms his father and leads chariots and horsemen, all the elders of Egypt, in a seven-day lamentation at the threshingfloor of Atad — so grievous the Canaanites name it Abelmizraim — before burying Jacob in Machpelah. Then the brothers, fearing revenge, send word of Jacob's command; Joseph weeps and answers 'am I in the place of God?' Dying at 110, Joseph takes an oath of the children of Israel that God will surely visit them and they shall carry up his bones from hence — the oath that Exodus and Joshua will honor.
summary.zh: 約瑟以香料薰父遺體，率法老諸臣與車馬，在約旦河外的亞達禾場哀哭七日，迦南人驚呼「這是埃及人一場極大的哀哭」，遂名亞伯麥西。雅各葬於麥比拉。諸兄懼報復遣使求赦，約瑟哭泣而答「我豈能代替神呢」。約瑟享壽一百一十歲而終，臨終令以色列人起誓：神必眷顧你們，你們要把我的骸骨從這裏搬上去。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The bones-oath frames the Exodus cycle that follows.

passages.text: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel. And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days. And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt, and there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.

And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days. And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abelmizraim, which is beyond Jordan. For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah.

And when Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him. And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.
